This appeal is filed by the State challenging the judgment and order dated 06.10.2015 passed in Sessions Case No.15048/2014 by the V Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Devanahalli, Bengaluru Rural District.

sentences.text: The respondents were charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Section 498(A), 307 of IPC r/w Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (hereinafter referred to as 'DP Act' for the sake of brevity).

2. The prosecution's case unfolds as follows: Accused No.1, having solemnized his marriage with PW8 (Muskan @ Noor-A-Chasma) on 25.08.2013, stands accused of NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB engaging in the commission of offences.

At the time of their matrimonial union, the parents of PW8 in compliance with prevailing dowry customs, bestowed upon the accused a dowry comprising a sum of Rs.40,000/- in cash, along with clothing and assorted valuables collectively appraised at Rs.60,000/-.
Additionally, PW8 was endowed with jewellery valued at Rs.1,50,000/- to symbolize her marital bond with accused No.1.
Subsequent to their union, PW8 assumed residence alongside accused No.1, accused No.2, accused No.3 (the parents of accused No.1), and accused No.4 (the sister of accused No.1) in Avathi.

Notwithstanding an initial period of two months characterized by amicable conduct, the accused allegedly embarked upon a course of conduct aimed at subjecting PW8 to relentless harassment, ostensibly in pursuit of further dowry.

In response to the relentless coercion, PW8 sought temporary refuge at her parental abode and on multiple occasions, remitted an additional sum of Rs.10,000/- in cash as dowry payments to the accused.
Regrettably, PW8's father's demise further exacerbated her NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB predicament.

Nevertheless, the accused allegedly undeterred by the attendant circumstances, continued their oppressive treatment of PW8, coercively demanding additional dowry despite her pleas of financial incapacity stemming from her family's modest means of subsistence through a small tea shop, without surplus funds to satisfy their demands.
3. Following PW8's refusal to comply with the demands of accused for additional dowry, resulted in their discontentment.
On the night of 29.12.2013, around 11:00 P.M., all the four accused individuals confronted PW8, accusing her of playing games and dramas, ominously threatened to end her life.
A quarrel ensued, during which the accused threatened her for life and their intention to cause her harm.
In furtherance of their alleged common objective, the accused procured a plastic can filled with kerosene.
Accused Nos.3 and 4 held PW8's limbs, while accused Nos.1 and 2 proceeded to pour kerosene on her and ignited it using a matchstick.

The resulting burns NC:

2 2023:KHC:21500-DB inflicted intense pain upon PW8, prompting her cries for help.

sentences.text: In a desperate attempt to protect herself, she instinctively clung onto accused No.2 causing him some injuries.

Understanding the legal consequences and fearing the initiation of criminal proceedings, the accused extinguished the flames and promptly arranged for shifting of PW8 to Victoria Hospital in an ambulance.
Thereafter, PW8 was admitted to Victoria Hospital as an inpatient, her severe burn injuries rendering her unable to narrate the incident's details to either the authorities or her relatives.
4. Following her discharge from the hospital, she was taken to her parental home.
Subsequently, on 15.02.2014 PW8 lodged a written complaint (Ex.P-6) with Vijayapura police, documenting the sequence of events surrounding the incident.
PW13-N.Shivanna received FIR on 15.02.2014 and on that basis, registered the case in Crime No.21/2014 and submitted the FIR to the Court and his superior officers.
After completion of investigation, PW12 - Circle NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB Police Inspector of Vijaypura Circle has submitted a charge sheet against the accused for the alleged offences.

5. To prove the case of prosecution, in all 13 witnesses were examined as PW1 to PW13, got 17 documents marked as Exs.P-1 to P-17, but Ex.P-5 is not marked as observed by the trial court in para 11 of the judgment and 2 material objects were marked as MOs.1 and 2.
6.

On closure of prosecution side evidence, the statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. for the incriminating circumstances were put to the accused, the accused have totally denied the evidence of prosecution witnesses.
However, they have not chosen to lead any defence on their behalf, but the accused have submitted that accused No.1 was not in the house on the date of alleged accident.
Further it is stated that due to stove burst in the house of accused Nos.2 and 3, the injured has sustained burnt injuries.
Accused No.4 was not in the house as on the date of alleged incident only to extract money false complaint is filed.
The trial court after hearing NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB the submissions made by the counsel has passed this impugned judgment of acquittal.
Being aggrieved by this judgment of acquittal the State has preferred this appeal.
7. Sri
. K.S.Abhijit, learned HCGP has argued that the judgment and order of acquittal rendered by the trial court is in direct contradiction to the established law, factual evidence, and the record.
It is contended that the Learned Sessions Judge failed to appropriately assess the evidence, particularly that of PW8 - complainant who suffered injuries, in its correct context.
Additionally, the trial court neglected to give due consideration to the testimonies of PW11 to PW13.
The trial court's justification for acquitting the accused based on a perceived delay in filing the complaint is deemed invalid.
It is asserted that the victim, who was an inpatient for 20 days receiving treatment for burn injuries, was unable to promptly file the complaint due to her condition and inability to communicate.
Furthermore, the trial court overlooked the fact that the accused provided false accounts, as evidenced by Exs.P-3 NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB and P-6, in an attempt to evade legal repercussions.

The trial court also failed to acknowledge the clear evidence presented in Ex.P-4,
which unequivocally refutes any claims of a stove burst.
Moreover, it is argued that the trial court did not appropriately consider the probabilities and draw logical inferences based on the available evidence.

Consequently, the impugned judgment is deemed unlawful, erroneous and should be State Of Karnataka vs Sajjad Pasha on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70689809/
3 overturned.

sentences.text: The appellant seeks the allowance of this appeal on these grounds.

8. Per contra, Sri.N.S.Sampangi Ramaiah, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent/accused has submitted his arguments that the trial court has appreciated the evidence on record in a proper and perspective manner and has passed the impugned judgment, which is in accordance with the law and facts.
Absolutely there are no materials to interfere with the impugned judgment of acquittal.
On all these grounds sought for dismissal of this appeal.

On hearing the arguments of both sides and on perusal of records the following points would arise for our consideration:
(1) Whether the prosecution has made out grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and order of acquittal?
(2) What order?

10. Our answer to the above points are as follows:
(1) In the negative (2) As per final order RE. POINT NO.1:
11.
On perusal of evidence placed before the Court, it is clear that there is no dispute that accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents and accused No.4 is sister of accused No.1.
It is also not in dispute that accused No.1 married PW8 - Smt.Muskan on 25.08.2013.
It is the case of the prosecution that for the sake of dowry, accused Nos.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention to murder PW8, poured kerosene on her and lit fire.
As a result, she sustained burn injuries.
Accused have taken defence that PW8 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB sustained burn injuries because of stove burst in the house on the date of alleged incident.
From these facts, one point is clear that PW8 sustained burn injuries due to stove burst which is accidental.
In this regard, the trial court has given finding that it is accidental.
12. The alleged incident took place on 29.12.2013 and Ex.P-6 - complaint was filed on 15.02.2014.
There is a delay of 48 days.

On the basis of complaint, the IO registered the case in Crime No.21/2014 against accused Nos.1 to 4 for the commission of offences punishable under Section 307, 498(A) r/w 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the DP Act and submitted the FIR to the Court as per Ex.P- 17.
In Column No.3(c) of FIR it is stated that since the complainant was taking treatment in the hospital she could not file the complaint.

Soon after the alleged incident, PW8 - Muskan was admitted to the hospital with the help of one Maula Khan with the history of burn injuries due to stove burst on 28.12.2013 at about 10.00 p.m. at home.

The wound - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB certificate reveals that the patient was conscious and oriented and she had sustained following injuries :
(1) Burns present over face, neck, B/L forearm and bilateral thighs As per inpatient case sheet (2) 2 to 8 degree burns 48% accidental thermal burn with facial burns.
13.
The medical expert has rendered an opinion stating that the injuries suffered by the complainant are severe and recent.
It is crucial to note that during the cross- examination, PW8 explicitly asserted her ability to speak at the time of discharge from Victoria Hospital.
Importantly, she did not disclose to the doctor that the accused individuals had allegedly poured kerosene and ignited a fire, resulting in her burn injuries.
Subsequent to her release from Victoria Hospital, PW8 initially went to her husband's residence and subsequently returned to her parents house after a few days.

14. Exhibit P-3 and the testimony of PW3, Dr. Rajareddy, who treated PW8, clearly establish that PW8 was admitted - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB to the hospital on 28.12.2013 at 10:00 p.m. citing a history of burn injuries caused by a stove burst in her house.
The injured party was brought to the hospital by an individual named Maula Khan.

Furthermore, Dr. Rajareddy testified regarding the injuries depicted in Exhibit P-3, stating that PW8 sustained burn injuries amounting to 48% of her body and received medical treatment from 29.12.2013 to 20.01.2014.
Dr.Rajareddy also affirmed that PW8 was conscious and able to communicate at the time of admission, understanding her surroundings.

Additionally, Dr. Rajareddy confirmed that he informed the police station situated within the premises of Victoria Hospital about the admission of the injured party with a history of burn injuries caused by a stove burst, as recorded in the police intimation book.
15. The collective evidence presented by PW3 and the contents of Ex.P-3 indicate that PW8 was in an oriented and conscious state, capable of speech.
Consequently, she provided a history consistent with sustaining burn injuries - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB due to a stove burst in her own residence.
Notably, despite PW8's capacity for communication and consciousness, she did not disclose anything regarding the alleged actions of the accused until her discharge from the hospital.
Even after her release, she delayed lodging a complaint with the police until 16.02.2014.
Ex.P-16 - discharge summary corroborates that PW8 was discharged from the hospital on 20.01.2014.
Subsequently, from 21.01.2014 to 15.02.2014 neither PW8 nor her relatives filed any complaint against the accused.

Regrettably, the IO failed to State Of Karnataka vs Sajjad Pasha on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70689809/
5 offer any explanation for the delay in filing the complaint during this period i.e., from 21.01.2014 15.02.2014.

sentences.text: 16. If the accused persons had truly conspired to pour kerosene on PW8, ignite fire, subject her to physical and mental harassment and demand dowry, a prudent woman like PW8 would have disclosed these allegations to the attending medical officer without delay.

However, in the present case, PW8 refrained from disclosing any such details to the medical professional during her - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB hospitalization or immediately following her discharge.
Instead, she consistently maintained that her burn injuries resulted from a stove burst in her own residence, as duly noted by the treating doctor in the appropriate register.
17. It is the defence of accused persons that after the incident PW8 and her brother tried to extract money from the accused and they refused to pay money to them.
Therefore, relatives of PW8 filed a false case against the accused.
Looking to the other circumstances and strained relationship between the parties, delay in filing the complaint is fatal to the case of prosecution.
There were chances that PW8 and her relatives deliberated and discussed and thereafter filed a complaint.
In Ex.P-6 - complaint nothing is stated about demand for dowry prior to marriage.
Even it is not stated that marriage talks were held and in the said marriage talks, accused demanded to pay dowry in the form of cash and valuable articles.

It appears subsequent to filing of Ex.P-6, new case was made out that even prior to marriage, marriage talks were held,
- 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB accused demanded dowry worth more than Rs.1,50,000/- in the form of gold and cash.
Ex.P-6 was filed after the delay of 48 days from the date of incident.
No such case is made out in Ex.P-6.
According to PW8, in her cross- examination, she says that it was prepared with the help of her brother, mother and uncle inspite of that no such allegations are mentioned in Ex.P-6.
Therefore, evidence of PW8 about said allegation is not reliable.
18. As per PW8's testimony, the accused persons rescued her and promptly transported her to the hospital for medical treatment.

It can be observed that if the accused had a motive to murder her,
their natural course of action would have been to flee the scene, rather than making efforts to extinguish the fire and rushing her to the hospital.
A prudent person would consider that if the victim survived, she might file a complaint against them subjecting them to prosecution.
These circumstances raise doubts regarding the prosecution's case.

Moreover, if the accused had indeed committed the alleged offences, as - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB stated in the complaint and by PW8, it is unlikely that she would have returned to her husband's residence after her discharge from the hospital.

It is noteworthy that PW8 State Of Karnataka vs Sajjad Pasha on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70689809/
6 resided there for a brief period before subsequently opting to return to her parents home, only then lodging a complaint with the police as per Ex.P-6.

sentences.text:
The conduct exhibited by PW8 is uncharacteristic,
incredulous and lacking in credibility.
It deviates from the conduct one would expect from an ordinary prudent individual.
Consequently, the prosecution has failed to provide a satisfactory explanation for the considerable and abnormal delay in filing the complaint.
Consequently, PW8's testimony raises doubts concerning the veracity of the accused alleged actions.

19. Trial court has elaborately discussed about the evidence of PW5 to PW7 and PW9 and close relatives of PW8 and came to the conclusion that the evidence of said witnesses cannot be believed as there is no consistency in their evidence as to the harassment and as also demand of - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB dowry as alleged by the prosecution.
Trial court has also rightly observed as to the conduct of the IO, who has not properly investigated the case in accordance with law.
20. "Ei incumbit probatio qui dicit, non qui negat"
This Latin maxim translates to "the burden of proof is on the one who declares, not on the one who denies."
It signifies that the prosecution bears the burden of proving the guilt of the accused and must present sufficient evidence to establish their case beyond a reasonable doubt.

The prosecution must fulfill its responsibilities diligently,
presenting compelling evidence, examining witnesses and addressing any legal defences raised by the accused.
However, the prosecution failed to meet the required burden of proof and the evidence is found to be not only insufficient but also unreliable.

Viewed from any angle that there is no legal evidence to prove that accused have committed the alleged commission of offences and that there is no cogent, corroborative trustworthy evidence before this Court.

The trial court has properly appreciated - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC:21500-DB the evidence on record and has recognised the accused's presumption of innocence and their right to be free from unwarranted conviction.
Hence, we do not find any materials to interfere with the impugned judgment of acquittal passed by the trial court.
Hence, we answer point No.1 is answered in the negative.

RE. POINT NO.2:
21.

For the aforesaid reasons and discussion, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (1) Appeal is dismissed.
(2) Registry is directed to transmit the records to the jurisdictional court along with the copy of this judgment.
